History of Present Illness:
This history was taken with the help of a ___ interpreter. 
The patient is a ___ yo ___ man with a history of 
CAD s/p POBA and overlapping BMS in RCA ___ and s/p POBA of 
instent occlusion of the RCA ___, HTN, DM2 on insulin, and 
dyslipidemia who presents with a 1 week history of intermittent 
chest pain.  He reports that he had a follow up appointment with 
___ cardiology NP on ___. At that time he complained of SOB 
with moderate exertion relieved by occasional NTG SL, and he was 
started on Imdur 30 daily to help relieve his SOB.  Since then, 
he reports continued dyspnea on exertion. Over the past week, he 
has had 3 episodes of chest pain.  At 9 am on the day of 
admission, he developed ___ chest tightness/pressure at rest 
at his left and right upper sternal borders that did not 
radiate. The pain was associated with SOB, but no diaphoresis, 
n/v. This chest pain was similar to the pain he had previously 
during his NSTEMI. He does also report a 1 day history of new 
lower extremity edema.    
.  
In the ED, vitals were temp 97.8, bp 191/81, HR 103, RR 18, SaO2 
100%RA. EKG showed sinus tachycardia with no ST-T changes.  CEs: 
TropT 0.05, CK 358, MB 11, and MBI 3.1  He was given NTG 0.3 SL 
x 1 and Morphine 4 mg IV x2 with resolution of CP. CXR showed no 
acute cardiopulmonary process. 
.  
He is currently chest pain free and denies SOB.
.
On review of systems, he denies any prior history of stroke, 
TIA, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, bleeding at the 
time of surgery, myalgias, joint pains, cough, hemoptysis, black 
stools or red stools. He denies recent fevers, chills or rigors. 
He denies exertional buttock or calf pain. All of the other 
review of systems were negative.

___ COMMENTS:     The initial angiography revealed a total 
occlusion at
the distal RCA stent that was previously POBA'd. In addition the 
Ramus
had a slightly more severe 90% lesion. Heparin and integrilin 
were
administered for anticoagulation. The strategy was to perform 
balloon
angioplasty of the RCA and stent the Ramus lesion.
JR4 Guide provided good support. Whisper wiress crossed into the 
distal
vessel with some manipulation. 1.5 X 15 mm Voyager balloon was 
used to
predilate the lesion at 6 atms with some distal differential 
expansion.
With wire repositioning the balloon could then be advanced 
further and
fully expanded in the distal lesion. Another set of inflations 
at 8 atms
was performed with a 2.0 X 20 mm Maverick balloon and at 18 atms 
in
stent. There was no residual stenosis and no dissection.
We then turned our attention to the Ramus. XBLAD 3.5 Guide 
provided
excellent support. Whisper wire crossed the lesion easily. 2.0 X 
20 mm
Maverick balloon was used to predilate the lesion at 6 atms. 2.5 
X 28 mm
Cypher DES was the deployed (underexpanded) at 4 atms and 
post-dilated
with a 2.25 X 20 mm Quantum Maverick balloon at 14 atms.
There was no residual stenosis and no dissection.
The patient left the cath lab in stable condition.
Right arteriotomy site was closed with a ___ Fr Mynx Vascular 
Closure
device.

he was started on heparin IV, and his aspirin, plavix, 
atorvastatin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and imdur were continued. 
The patient underwent cardiac catheterization on ___, which

(unchanged), and the RCA was totally occluded at the distal 
stent. He underwent successful POBA of the RCA with 2.0 mm 
balloon with no residual 
stenosis and no dissection, and successful stenting of the Ramus 
with a 2.5 X 28 mm Cypher DES with no residual stenosis.
